name: Ancient Oceans & Deep Sea
description: Evidence-led episodes about the ocean as a system through deep time - its chemistry, circulation, gateways, reefs and sea levels - built from named sections, platforms, cores and expeditions, with the analytical method that turns each object into a claim about the past ocean.

exclusions: Do not present a contested date, correlation or ocean mechanism as settled.
Do not build the episode on a sea creature; the subject is the water, the seabed and the record.
Do not narrate a palaeoceanographic reconstruction as if it were an observation.
Do not read a modern ocean measurement back into deep time without saying it is an analogue.
prompt_context: Build the episode on one bounded object and the record that carries it: a core section, a drill bit, a reef slab, an outcrop face, an expedition logbook, an isotope curve. Name the setting and the geological interval, explain the physical, chemical or biological process that acted on the water or the seabed, and say plainly how the claim is known. The subject is the ocean as a system and the record it left, not the animal that lived in it. Keep observation, inference, debate and speculation separate. Where a date, a mechanism or a correlation is contested, present the competing records rather than picking a winner.
compatibility_rules: Use only with the Deep Time Documentary Formula.
Keep the object, its setting and interval, the mechanism, and the evidence method in every assignment.
